claims.statement: GitHub webhook deliveries land on a single signed endpoint (POST /webhooks/github) that verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC, ignores unsupported event types, and dispatches accepted handlers as FastAPI background tasks.

Automatic review of PR first-review events and push events is scheduled only when the repository is opted into automatic review through is_review_repo_enabled, which fails soft: an unreachable enabled-repos store reads as not opted in and skips the review rather than erroring the webhook.
process_github_pr_ready skips auto-reviewing a draft PR unless the PR author's review_draft_prs profile flag (falling back to the team-wide default) enables draft reviews.

An explicit review request enters through trigger_pr_review_from_ref, which fetches PR metadata to resolve base/head SHAs, sets reviewer thread metadata with watch=True, posts a review-started comment, and dispatches a reviewer run; request_pr_review is the agent tool that parses a PR URL and invokes it.

Every review of a given PR runs on one deterministic thread id, reviewer_thread_id(owner, repo, pr_number), a UUIDv5 over '{owner}/{repo}/pr/{pr_number}/reviewer'; webhooks, the dashboard, and the reviewer re-derive it from the same identifiers, so changing the formula would orphan live threads.

Reviewer runs are dispatched with assistant_id='reviewer', which maps to the reviewer graph (agent.graphs.reviewer:traced_reviewer_agent), and the dispatched run id is stored on reviewer thread metadata via store_current_reviewer_run_id.

Persisted finding records are normalized on every read by coerce_finding, which folds legacy flat-singular GitHub-identity fields and a nested 'surface' record into canonical comment/thread ID lists plus a forward-only surface_state so the rest of the codebase never sees the legacy shape.

Findings writes use a locked read-modify-write layer: mutate_findings locks the pull-request finding state and writes only if the mutator changed data, replace_findings merges an incoming snapshot by ID so concurrently-added findings are not dropped, and append_finding de-duplicates by fingerprint against open findings.

When the reviewer thread backing findings storage does not exist, the storage layer raises ReviewerThreadMissingError and tools return a structured do-not-retry result (thread_missing_tool_result) instead of blindly retrying.

add_finding enforces in-diff-only discipline when a diff line set is available: it validates a line range against the file and side, rejects an out-of-diff finding with success:false and in_diff:false and an explicit do-not-retry message, while file-level findings are accepted but cannot render as inline comments.

add_finding requires a non-default generated title, validates severity/confidence/side enums, and clips suggestions longer than the 4-line cap (MAX_SUGGESTION_LINES), dropping the suggestion while keeping the description-only finding.

Severity is ordered low < medium < high < critical; filter_findings_for_publish surfaces only open findings at or above the severity threshold (default medium), ordered first by explicit rank and then severity-descending/file/line, with ordinary publication capped at REVIEW_FINDING_CAP (6). Confidence is recorded but does not gate publication.

publish_review posts eligible findings as a single GitHub PR Review with inline comments (path, line, side, metadata marker, and optional fenced suggestion) and a host-formatted summary body; on a re-review it drops already-commented findings and limits publication to findings first seen at the current head.

publish_review resolves the effective head SHA from thread metadata because a mid-run push can make the run configuration stale, then records GitHub review and comment identities together and backfills thread IDs so surfaced findings remain reconcilable.

publish_review explicitly handles edge cases: eval mode is a dry run, an empty re-review with an existing Open SWE summary skips another summary while resolving fixed threads and advancing last_reviewed_sha, and a 422 unresolved-anchor rejection removes identifiable invalid findings and retries the remaining batch once before returning unresolvable_findings.

process_github_pr_close toggles the reviewer thread watch flag on PR lifecycle transitions: reopened re-enables watch, closed disables it, and converted_to_draft disables watch only when the author's effective draft-review setting is off.

process_github_push_event re-triggers the reviewer only for a watched reviewer thread whose PR head actually changed; it short-circuits when the head equals last_reviewed_sha, the thread is not watching, or the diff is proven unchanged, in which case it advances last_reviewed_sha and creates-then-settles a 'No new changes to review' check on the new head.

On a changed-diff push, or a ready_for_review event after a prior review, a re-review is dispatched with re_review=True and a prompt to reconcile existing findings against the new diff, add net-new findings, and call publish_review; the ready_for_review path skips dispatch when head_sha equals last_reviewed_sha.

reconcile_findings_with_review_threads syncs tracked findings with live GitHub review threads: it matches bot-authored markers before stored identities, backfills comment/thread identity and marks findings surfaced, records the latest human reply for reassessment, and moves an open finding to resolved only when all matched threads are resolved.

process_github_review_finding_reply routes a non-bot reply to an Open SWE review comment back to the reviewer graph: it reconciles findings, matches the parent comment ID to a finding, records the reply as a FindingInteraction flagged needs_reassessment, and dispatches a reviewer run with reviewer_event='finding_reply'.

Automatic first-review and push dispatch paths create an 'Open SWE Review' GitHub check run and store review_check_run_id in thread metadata; settle_review_check_run clears the ID only after a successful PATCH and stashes the intended result in review_check_pending_result so a transient failure can be retried with the real conclusion.

If a reviewer run ends without publishing, the settle_review_check_on_exit after-agent middleware closes the still-open review check as neutral; it reuses a stashed review_check_pending_result when publish finished but its completion PATCH failed.

tests/reviewer covers automatic PR admission and drafts, push-watch and unchanged-diff behavior, PostgreSQL finding storage and tool validation, GitHub reconciliation, and review publication/status behavior.

Reviewer preparation obtains the applicable GitHub token, prepares a replaceable per-thread sandbox and checkout before the model runs, materializes review context, and injects the per-file/per-side changed-line set used to validate finding anchors locally.

The reviewer prompt treats PR descriptions and existing review-thread bodies as untrusted data, delimits them to resist prompt injection, and directs the reviewer to reject style-only, speculative, pre-existing, and out-of-diff findings while allowing organization, repository, and base-branch conventions to refine review criteria.

Reviewer thread metadata owns PR identity, live and last-reviewed SHAs, watch state, and check/run coordination, while findings are stored in PostgreSQL under the linked pull request; legacy metadata findings are copied into PostgreSQL on first access.
